articles.originalTitle: Morning Pages: James Cahill reads from 'The Beverly Hills Housewife' | Events - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Author James Cahill to Read at the National Gallery in London
articles.excerpt: Author, critic and art historian James Cahill will read from his latest book on David Hockney during the second event of the Morning Pages series.
articles.content: Author, critic and art historian Dr. James Cahill will appear as a guest for the second installment of the Morning Pages series at the National Gallery in London. During the special gathering in the Supporters' House Salon, Cahill will discuss and read from his book titled 'The Beverly Hills Housewife: Hockney's Californian Muse and the World Beyond the Pool', published by Thames & Hudson. The event offers attendees an opportunity to gain insight directly from the author regarding David Hockney's world and artistic legacy. The reading will be followed by a question-and-answer session, along with an opportunity to purchase and have copies signed by the author. Based between London and Los Angeles, Cahill's previous literary works include his debut novel 'Tiepolo Blue', shortlisted for the Author's Club Best First Novel Award, and his second novel 'The Violet Health'. He also contributes articles to publications including Artforum, the Burlington Magazine, the Financial Times, the Los Angeles Times, the Spectator and the Times Literary Supplement.

articles.originalTitle: ‘Strain and Resilience’: Alma Allen at Perrotin Paris - ArtReview
articles.title: Alma Allen Presents First Solo Exhibition at Perrotin in Paris
articles.excerpt: Perrotin is hosting Alma Allen's first solo exhibition featuring monumental bronze sculptures at its Paris space. Running through December 19, the presentation brings together new works focusing on touch, transformation, and perception.
articles.content: Perrotin in Paris is presenting Alma Allen's first solo exhibition with the gallery, featuring a new body of monumental bronze sculptures. On view at the space on impasse Saint-Claude from October 17 through December 19, the exhibition introduces works that explore touch, transformation, memory, and perception. Each sculpture bears the designation Not Yet Titled, reflecting the artist's belief that meaning should remain open. Working with string, clay, or wax, the self-taught sculptor develops small models by hand, a practice originating from his teenage years in Utah. Once completed, these models are scanned, enlarged, and cast in bronze at his home foundry. The resulting twisted and elastic sculptures communicate both strain and resilience, recalling nautical knots and lengths of rope. Alongside freestanding works, the exhibition features bronze wall reliefs with ridged surfaces kneaded by hand. Designed to weather and evolve over time, the bronzes draw together botanical, religious, and art-historical references, connecting the natural world with spiritual traditions. Allen describes his sculptures as apparitions emerging from a curiosity to look beyond the visible surface of reality.

articles.originalTitle: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190m at Sotheby’s following Nazi loot claims - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Van Gogh painting achieves record auction price in New York
articles.excerpt: A late work by Vincent van Gogh sold for 190.4 million dollars including fees at Sotheby's, breaking the artist's auction record. A settlement regarding Nazi-era provenance claims had been reached just prior to the sale.
articles.content: One of Vincent van Gogh's final paintings from 1890, Blossoming Chestnut Trees, sold for 165 million dollars at a Sotheby's New York auction, reaching 190.4 million dollars with fees to surpass the artist's previous auction record. Long kept out of public view within the Blaquier-Arrieta collection, the artwork's sale followed a settlement announced by Sotheby's a day prior regarding its Nazi-era provenance claims. After nearly five minutes of bidding, the guaranteed work went to a room bidder, becoming the second most valuable object ever sold at Sotheby's. Back-to-back New York sales generated a combined 777.8 million dollars with fees, featuring additional auction records for Mary Cassatt and Aaron Douglas. Aaron Douglas's Harriet Tubman achieved 14.48 million dollars after a seven-minute bidding battle, shattering the artist's previous benchmark. Meanwhile, Paul Cézanne's Arlequin fell short of its estimate at 111 million dollars with fees, and several other lots across the evening's sessions failed to meet expectations or were withdrawn from the auction.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Constantinople to Istanbul Exhibition at the V&A
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting the Constantinople to Istanbul exhibition, exploring 1600 years of artistic production from the Roman Empire to the Ottomans. The event runs until 9 May 2027.
articles.content: Hosted at V&A South Kensington in London, the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition explores 1600 years of artistic heritage spanning from AD 330 to 1922. Examining the art and design traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires, the exhibition remains open until 9 May 2027. It showcases more than 200 objects, including textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, jewelry, sculptures, and manuscripts. The exhibition is organized into four main sections. The opening section, Roman Beginnings, covers the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire and highlights structures such as the Hippodrome. Heaven and Earth explores Christian art and Byzantine imperial authority, while Power and Reach examines how the Ottoman court projected authority through luxury materials and grand processions. The final section, Life in the City, presents the city as a cosmopolitan center, detailing daily urban rhythms and 19th-century stylistic shifts. The exhibition also traces the enduring influence of Byzantine and Ottoman art on 19th-century Europe, featuring works by figures such as William Morris.

articles.originalTitle: BIG stacks timber volumes with alpine views for new neighborhood in switzerland - Designboom
articles.title: Bjarke Ingels Group Unveils Timber Neighborhood Design for Thun, Switzerland
articles.excerpt: Bjarke Ingels Group has unveiled plans for Nachwachsende Stadt, a 13,000-square-meter development comprising four timber buildings in Thun, Switzerland.
articles.content: Bjarke Ingels Group has revealed plans for Nachwachsende Stadt, a new 13,000-square-meter timber development located in Thun, Switzerland. Selected through a competition organized by Frutiger AG and the city of Thun, the scheme includes two hotels and residential buildings featuring stacked wooden volumes and deep window grids. The development allocates approximately 6,500 square meters for residential uses, 6,000 square meters for hotels, and 400 square meters for commercial activities. At the southwest corner, a combined three-star and four-star hotel structure features shared amenity spaces, outdoor terraces, and a rooftop restaurant. The eastern residential buildings frame a shared garden courtyard with flexible apartment layouts and private balconies. Timber is utilized across all four structures to reduce embodied carbon, with components engineered for future disassembly and reuse. Sustainability measures also include green roofs, rainwater retention systems, and approximately 1,800 square meters of photovoltaic panels. The development is targeting Switzerland's SNBS Gold certification, with construction on the first buildings possible starting in 2028.

articles.originalTitle: Mary Miss’s Long Fight to Keep Public Art Alive - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Mary Miss and Her Long Career Shaping the Boundaries of Public Art
articles.excerpt: Pioneering public artist Mary Miss reflects on decades of creating site-specific works that challenge conventional definitions of art, architecture, and landscape in the modern world.
articles.content: Born in 1944, Mary Miss emerged as a pioneering figure in the public art revolution of the 1980s, moving away from static monuments toward participatory installations. Among her most celebrated works is South Cove, a waterside park created between 1984 and 1987 in Manhattan's Battery Park City, which integrated natural elements with maritime history. Throughout a career spanning decades, Miss encountered bureaucratic obstacles, budget limitations, nonpayment, and the dismantling of signature pieces. Rather than deterring her, these challenges prompted her to adapt her approach, culminating in ongoing community-focused initiatives such as her City as Living Laboratory project. From her early outdoor constructions in Colorado to urban interventions that incorporated deep site research, her practice consistently challenged conventional definitions of public art. Her 1977 installation Perimeters, Pavilions, Decoys notably helped shape critical discourse regarding sculpture in the expanded field, engaging directly with architecture and landscape. Despite shifts in public funding and political climates, Miss maintains a steadfast dedication to fostering connections and dialogue through art created specifically for public spaces.

articles.originalTitle: EU Countries Renew Call To Exclude Russia from Venice Ahead of 2027 Architecture Biennale - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Ten European Union Countries Renew Call to Exclude Russia from Venice
articles.excerpt: Ten European Union countries are demanding sustained efforts from the European Commission to keep Russia out of the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennial. Signatories of a diplomatic note state that Moscow's presence risks normalizing its war on Ukraine.
articles.content: According to Rapporteur, ten European Union countries are demanding sustained efforts from the European Commission to keep Russia out of the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennial. A diplomatic note signed by Poland, Austria, Croatia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, and Sweden states that Moscow's presence on the cultural stage risks normalizing its war on Ukraine, noting there should be no room for normalisation without a just and lasting peace. The group urged the European Union to take measures ahead of a meeting of culture ministers. The European Commission previously suspended a €2 million grant to the Biennale after organizers resisted calls to exclude Moscow, with Biennale president Pietrangelo Buttafuoco defending his decision by stating the organization rejects censorship. During the 2026 art exhibition, the Russian Pavilion became the target of protests and temporary closures across multiple national pavilions. The upcoming Venice Architecture Biennale, curated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu under the theme 'Do Architecture — For the Possibility of Coexistence Facing a Real Reality,' is scheduled to open to the public on May 8, 2027, and run through November 21, 2027.

articles.originalTitle: AOM Higher Education/Research: Utah State University Kem & Carolyn Gardner Learning & Leadership Building - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Utah State University Building Receives Mountain States Award
articles.excerpt: The Utah State University Kem & Carolyn Gardner Learning & Leadership Building has received an Award of Merit in the ENR Mountain States Best Projects competition.
articles.content: The Utah State University Kem & Carolyn Gardner Learning & Leadership Building has received an Award of Merit in the ENR Mountain States Best Projects competition. Submitted by Jacobsen Construction, the project serves as a 44,658-square-foot, three-story academic facility in Logan, Utah, merging five academic centers from the university's Jon M. Huntsman School of Business under one roof. Situated on a constrained site near Highway 89 alongside two other active construction projects, the building was constructed with Jacobsen serving as general contractor and MHTN Architects as lead design firm. The facility features flexible, technology-rich learning spaces designed around a hybrid steel and mass timber system, making it the university's first mass timber building. Exposed glulam columns and cross-laminated timber decking created a light-filled interior inspired by nearby Logan Canyon. The structural system supports the university's carbon neutrality goal by 2040. During design development, teams coordinated with Timberlab to conceal conduit and ductwork within cavities, preserving the visual continuity of the timber.

articles.originalTitle: Nan Goldin to debut new film exploring nature and extinction in first UK solo museum show in over two decades - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Nan Goldin to debut new film exploring nature and extinction in London exhibition
articles.excerpt: American photographer Nan Goldin will premiere a new film exploring nature and extinction at London's Hayward Gallery in her first UK solo museum exhibition in over two decades.
articles.content: American photographer Nan Goldin will debut her new film exploring nature and impending extinction at London's Hayward Gallery, marking her first institutional solo exhibition in the UK in over two decades. According to chief curator Rachel Thomas, the exhibition extends Goldin's compassionate focus from queer communities and chosen family to the broader natural world. Part of the Southbank Centre's 75th-anniversary programme, the four-year-in-the-making show presents recent and new work rather than serving as a retrospective. The gallery's centrepiece will be the premiere of You never did anything wrong, Part II, created alongside filmmaker David Sherman, which draws on 1960s and 1970s nature documentaries and damaged soundtracks with a score by British musician Mica Levi. The exhibition also features the first part of the project centering on a solar eclipse, alongside other series such as Stendhal Syndrome, which places portraits of friends and lovers in dialogue with classical art, and Memory Lost, which addresses opioid addiction and Goldin's activism. The exhibition runs from 24 November to 14 March 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires – exhibition large print guide - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Publishes Constantinople Exhibition Guide
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum has published a comprehensive exhibition guide examining the rich history, art, and architecture of the city that served as capital to two empires.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum has issued an exhibition guide detailing the historical transformation from Constantinople to Istanbul. In 324 CE, Emperor Constantine I selected the ancient site as his new capital, naming it Nova Roma before it became known as Constantinople. The settlement served as the capital of the Byzantine Empire until 1453, and subsequently as the Ottoman capital until 1922. Situated at the junction of Asia and Europe, the metropolis flourished through trade, taxation, and loot, funding outstanding public works and architecture. The exhibition explores the city's vital engineering feats, including the 5.6-kilometer Theodosian Walls and the 4th-century Aqueduct of Valens. Religious life transitioned through Roman paganism, Christianity, and Islam, while a diverse population of merchants and craftspeople inhabited the urban center. The guide highlights various historical objects, such as ivory plaques of Christ Pantocrator, Hâfız Osman's calligraphy describing the Prophet Muhammad, restoration inscriptions of Emperor Michael III, and cameos made from rock crystal, lapis lazuli, and amethyst. These artifacts demonstrate the two distinct traditions of art and design practiced within the city across its long imperial history.

articles.originalTitle: 2026 Record Awards: Jules & Jim Bridges by Dietmar Feichtinger Architects - Architectural Record
articles.title: New Pedestrian Bridges Reconnect Historic Centers Across the Seine Near Paris
articles.excerpt: Designed by Dietmar Feichtinger Architectes, the Jules and Jim bridges restore a historic link destroyed in World War II, creating a continuous pedestrian and bicycle route connecting Mantes-la-Jolie and Limay.
articles.content: Constructed over the Seine River in France, a pair of pedestrian footbridges named Jules and Jim reconnect the historic centers of Mantes-la-Jolie and Limay. Located about 30 miles west of Paris, the project restores a link lost with the destruction of a medieval bridge during World War II. The design introduces two contemporary crossings, establishing a continuous pedestrian and bicycle route connecting public spaces, parks, and cultural landmarks. The 660-foot Jules bridge spans from Mantes to the Île aux Dames in the middle of the river, utilizing existing masonry piers of the adjacent vehicular crossing to minimize riverbed disruption. The 80-foot Jim bridge connects the island and Limay by spanning extant sections of the medieval crossing. Named after a 1962 film by François Truffaut, the project transforms a historical rupture into a renewed connection. The client for the initiative is the Syndicat Mixte d’aménagement, de gestion et d’entretien des berges de la Seine et Oise. Dietmar Feichtinger Architectes served as the architect, with engineering by Terrell SAS, historic monument consulting by ALEP Architectes, and lighting design by Coup d’éclat.

articles.originalTitle: Construction underway on Jean Nouvel’s landmark opera house in China - Dezeen
articles.title: Construction Progress Visualized for Jean Nouvel's Shenzhen Opera House in China
articles.excerpt: Ateliers Jean Nouvel has released photographs revealing construction progress on the 250,000-square-meter Shenzhen Opera House in China.
articles.content: French architecture studio Ateliers Jean Nouvel has shared photographs revealing ongoing construction on the Shenzhen Opera House in China, which is scheduled for completion in 2028. Situated on the Shekou Peninsula overlooking Shenzhen Bay, the 250,000-square-meter cultural landmark features an elongated, wavy roofscape reflecting its waterfront setting. The complex stems from a winning competition entry designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Jean Nouvel's studio. Facilities within the expansive development include a 2,300-seat concert hall with a horseshoe-shaped plan, an 1,800-seat theatre, an 800-seat venue, and a 400-seat multifunctional theatre. Additional spaces comprise cultural areas, backstage facilities, offices, and performer apartments. To connect the structure visually with the surrounding water, interior spaces are planned to feature iridescent materials such as mother-of-pearl. Nouvel previously described the use of lustrous nacreous reflections as a poetic representation of the meeting between the sea, light, and auditorium spaces.

articles.originalTitle: Dezeen Awards 2026 architecture project of the year revealed - Dezeen

articles.content: Nineteen architecture category winners across 11 different countries were announced during the ninth annual Dezeen Awards ceremony in London. articles.originalTitle: Construction Starts on $246M Niagara Falls Power Station Hotel Conversion - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Historic Niagara Falls Power Station Converted Into Luxury Hotel
articles.excerpt: Construction has begun on a privately financed redevelopment exceeding 246 million dollars to convert the century-old Toronto Power Generating Station near Niagara Falls into a hotel and visitor complex, with completion expected in 2029.
articles.content: Construction has commenced on a redevelopment exceeding 246 million dollars to transform the century-old Toronto Power Generating Station overlooking Niagara Falls into a hotel and visitor complex. Owned by the Ontario provincial agency Niagara Parks, the historic facility is being redeveloped by Toronto Power Hotel Inc., a partnership overseeing the privately financed project. Deltera Contracting Inc. serves as the general contractor, with +VG Architects and MT Planners on the project team. Designed by E.J. Lennox, the steel-frame building opened in 1906 and operated until 1974. The preservation effort will maintain key architectural features while adding a five-star hotel, multiple restaurants, a wellness spa, event facilities, an art gallery, a museum, and public viewing areas. Audited financial statements indicate that approximately 6.72 million dollars in stabilization obligations were transferred to Society Land Holdings Inc. under a long-term lease. Substantial construction completion is anticipated in 2029, with the hotel opening scheduled for 2030.

articles.originalTitle: Building a Permanent Home for a Space Shuttle Was an Engineering Endeavor - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Permanent Exhibition Center Unveiled for Retired Space Shuttle Endeavor
articles.excerpt: The 450-million-dollar Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center at the California Science Center in Los Angeles has opened to house the vertically positioned space shuttle Endeavor.
articles.content: The Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center has opened at the California Science Center in Los Angeles, housing the retired space shuttle Endeavor. Having completed its final mission in June 2011, Endeavor is the world's only space shuttle exhibited in the vertical launch configuration, complete with boosters and an external tank. Designed by ZGF Architects and built by general contractor MATT Construction, the 200-foot-tall curvilinear stainless-steel structure required complex seismic analysis and intricate steel node assembly. Engineering teams utilized specialized scaffolding and commercial cranes to maneuver components without damaging the fragile thermal silica tiles on the shuttle. To comply with Exposition Park campus height limits, the facility was designed 25 feet below grade, completing a multi-year effort to establish a permanent home for the spacecraft.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach: Highlights - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach 2026 Gathers the International Art World
articles.excerpt: Held at the cultural crossroads of the Americas from December 4 to 6, 2026, Art Basel Miami Beach unites leading figures in modern and contemporary art with digital art projects and discussions.
articles.content: Situated at the cultural crossroads of the Americas, Art Basel Miami Beach prepares to unite the international art world from December 4 to 6, 2026. The region's leading art fair brings together established galleries, emerging talent, and daring new presentations, spanning Modern masterpieces, contemporary trailblazers, and new frontiers in digital art. The fair's digital art platform, Zero 10, returns with Generation, its largest presentation to date, curated by Karen Archey and Eli Scheinman. Spanning 19 projects, the exhibition explores connections between digital technologies and traditional art forms through works by Sarah Meyohas, Jon Rafman, and Studio DRIFT. Refik Anadol's collaboration with the Yawanawá community transforms Amazonian artwork and weather data into digital imagery, while Harm van den Dorpel's work draws on historical geometric drawings. The Conversations talks program features discussions on patronage, the art market, and the intersection of art and technology. Panels include appearances by Jeff Koons, Julie Mehretu, Kevin Love, Crystal Dunn, Keith Rivers, and Swizz Beatz, with all sessions free and open to the public.

articles.originalTitle: Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA Receives the First Ambasz–MoMA Annual Prize for Nature–Reconciled Architecture - ArchDaily
articles.title: Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA Wins Inaugural MoMA Nature Prize
articles.excerpt: The Museum of Modern Art has selected Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA for the first Ambasz–MoMA Annual Prize for Nature–Reconciled Architecture for the Friendship Centre in Bangladesh.
articles.content: The Museum of Modern Art has selected Dhaka-based architectural office Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA as the recipient of the first Ambasz–MoMA Annual Prize for Nature–Reconciled Architecture for the Friendship Centre in Gaibandha, Bangladesh. Described by MoMA as the largest award for a single architecture project, the prize aims to recognize architectural practice while supporting tangible environmental action. The 200,000 dollar award is shared between the architect and the Fundación Gran Chaco, a nonprofit organization in Formosa, Argentina, which will plant trees in the Gran Chaco forest. Administered through the Emilio Ambasz Institute, the prize honors architecture that merges environmental adaptation, historical continuity, and community sensitivity. Completed in 2011 in the flood-prone Jamuna River delta, the Friendship Centre provides a rural training facility handcrafted mostly with local clay bricks, drawing spatial inspiration from the ancient city of Mahasthangarh. Selected from nearly 140 international projects by a five-member jury, the award will be presented during a ceremony at MoMA on December 12, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Fragonard Hosts Centenary Birthday Exhibition at the Paris Mint - WWD
articles.title: Fragonard Hosts Centenary Exhibition at the Paris Mint
articles.excerpt: Grasse-based fragrance and lifestyle brand Fragonard is opening a centenary exhibition featuring more than 250 works and objects at the Paris Mint.
articles.content: Frane-based fragrance and lifestyle brand Fragonard is celebrating its centenary with a major exhibition at the Paris Mint. Entitled "Fragonard: 100 Years of Collections and Savoir-Faire," the event gathers more than 250 works and objects from the house's heritage collection. The exhibition remains open to the public through Jan. 17, 2027. Company chief executive officer Agnès Costa Webster noted that paintings from the family's collection in Grasse have been brought to Paris for the first time. Hosted at the 18th-century Hôtel de la Monnaie, the multisensory exhibition features paintings, perfume bottles, historic garments, silverware, and personal grooming accessories. The scenography was conceived by Nathalie Crinière, while Givaudan perfumer Daniela Andrier formulated scents based on 18th-century recipes specifically for the event. Visitors can also explore an onsite boutique and attend fragrance-making workshops by reservation.

articles.originalTitle: Eight Dead, 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Eight Dead and 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Near Construction Site
articles.excerpt: An adjoining 96-year-old three-story building collapsed into an excavation site in Brooklyn, New York, leaving 8 people dead and 18 injured. Authorities have launched multiple investigations into the incident.
articles.content: On November 11, a three-story building collapsed into an adjoining excavation site in the Brooklyn borough of New York, resulting in 8 fatalities and 18 injuries. Officials confirmed the dead included two children and two construction workers, while the Fire Department concluded rescue operations on November 12. City records list Townhouse Builders as the general contractor for the project at 2625 Bedford Ave. A project geotechnical report had warned that abutting structures required underpinning and that construction-related vibrations could adversely affect neighboring properties. A March 5 preconstruction survey documented visible cracking at 1321 Flatbush Ave., rating its north masonry facade as poor and its other facades as fair. Area residents reported feeling heavy impacts and shaking while construction was underway next door. Mayor Zohran Mamdani ordered safety inspections at approximately 100 other construction sites linked to companies involved in the project. New York Attorney General Letitia James stated that the Buildings Department would conduct a full investigation, alongside a separate probe launched by Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez. The exact cause of the structural collapse remains undetermined pending the conclusion of ongoing investigations by municipal authorities.

articles.originalTitle: Designers’ Creative Freedom Unveiled at Molteni Museum Exhibit - WWD
articles.title: Molteni Museum Exhibition Unveils Creative Freedom for International Designers
articles.excerpt: The Molteni Museum in Giussano, Italy, has unveiled a new exhibition giving prominent architects and designers the creative freedom to produce expressive works using existing brand elements without commercial constraints.
articles.content: Hosted at the Molteni Compound in Giussano, Italy, the Molteni Museum opened a new exhibition designed to offer furniture industry creators the rare opportunity to produce expressive, unconstrained works. Using existing pieces from Molteni Group brands as a starting point, the showcase celebrates living creatives rather than historical icons, removing the traditional boundaries of commerce and engineering complexity. Participating practices and designers include Herzog & de Meuron, Jean Nouvel, Naoto Fukasawa, OMA, AMDL Circle, Foster + Partners Industrial Design, Patricia Urquiola, Ron Gilad, and Vincent Van Duysen. Israeli artist Ron Gilad created a poetic fountain with four faucets as a tribute to late designer Luca Meda, while Herzog & de Meuron reinterpreted a special-edition chair with playful, candy-colored inflatable cushions. Rotterdam-based OMA approached the Principles collection through material experimentation, joined by AMDL Circle's surreal interpretation of the MDL System. Accompanied by video installations produced by Muse Factory of Projects, the exhibition will remain on display at the museum for one year before embarking on an international tour to a to-be-determined roster of cities.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | TAREK EL-ARISS | Emptying the Jars of War, or How We Learned to Love Nature - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Tarek El-Ariss to Discuss War, Nature, and Water Politics at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Tarek El-Ariss will examine how crises alter perceptions of nature and reframe sustainability during a lecture at Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Tarek El-Ariss is scheduled to speak at an event during Biennale Arte 2026 on November 21, 2026. Taking place at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale from 16:00 to 17:30, the lecture will be introduced and moderated by Rasha Salti. The session addresses how crises and wars not only damage the environment but also unsettle perceptions of nature. Drawing from everyday scenes such as saving water jars for bathing during wartime in Lebanon, the discussion traces longer histories and mythologies of water and greenery from the Garden of Eden to Greek and Islamic traditions, while focusing on the oasis as a recurring fantasy. The lecture posits that environmental practices do not necessarily emerge from ethical choices, often arising instead through habit, fear, or the quest for survival. Sustainability is reframed as a negotiation that interrogates the politics of purity and control to imagine alternative futures. Admission to the event is free until venue capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: FRIEDA EKOTTO | Resilience Against Value: Authored Practices of Repair in Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Frieda Ekotto to Deliver Lecture at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale
articles.excerpt: Frieda Ekotto will deliver a lecture examining the repair practices in the works of Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama. The event takes place on November 20, 2026, at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale.
articles.content: Frieda Ekotto will present a lecture examining the gathering, wrapping, repairing, and regenerating actions central to the practices of Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama. The event is scheduled for November 20, 2026, from 16:00 to 17:30 at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale. The discussion explores processes that redirect materials, labor, and time toward connections between land, body, and community that extraction seeks to disrupt. These actions form a resilience rooted in acts of refusal. By framing disobedience as the foundation of resilience, the lecture recasts the work of both artists as a sustained challenge to damaging value systems, pointing toward a relational model of authorship. Rasha Salti will introduce and moderate the session. Admission to the venue is free until capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | RANA EL NEMR | The Newborn Birthchart - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Rana El Nemr Presents The Newborn Birthchart at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Rana El Nemr’s two-part installation, The Newborn Birthchart, is presented at the Arsenale during Biennale Arte 2026, inviting audiences to share communal stories and songs.
articles.content: Scheduled for 18 November 2026 from 11:00 to 11:30 at the Arsenale, the performance titled The Newborn Birthchart forms part of Biennale Arte 2026. Designed as an active threshold, the two-part installation registers each visit as a vibrational contribution to the work in space. Through readings, songs, incantations, and cues from the artwork's card deck, the performance invites the audience to communally harvest the stories and songs of swamps, canefields, sugar, resistance, and yearnings. Gathering to witness invisible footprints and evanescent potentialities, the performance initiates at the fringe of a six-meter recycled plastic curtain featuring a sunken sun and a protruding moon, forming a constellation for what is yet to be born. The participating performers are Maissa Alameldine, Mariamme Boctor, rana elnemr, Nour Kamel, and Farida Rehab. Attendance requires a valid admission ticket to Biennale Arte 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | ZIAD ANTAR | Bladder Diplomacy - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Ziad Antar Presents Bladder Diplomacy Lecture Performance at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Scheduled for Biennale Arte 2026, Bladder Diplomacy weaves together international diplomacy, agricultural habits in the eastern Mediterranean, and personal family stories through a satirical performance.
articles.content: La Biennale di Venezia hosts the lecture performance Bladder Diplomacy at Tese dei Soppalchi on 18 November 2026, running from 16:00 to 17:20. The event weaves stories of international diplomacy and the cultivation of potatoes and tomatoes in the eastern Mediterranean together with personal family narratives. The work examines radical interventions in the natural environment and nutritional habits introduced to the region by modernization and globalized agribusiness. Lebanese artists Ziad Antar, Hatem Imam, and Nayla Mabsout collaborate on the performance, drawing a satirical puzzle of malicious weeds, civil wars, and the resilience of indigenous seeds. The script is written by Ziad Antar, directed by Hatem Imam, and features video by Nayla Mabsout, with Ziad Antar and Nayla Mabsout performing. Visitors must hold a valid admission ticket to Biennale Arte 2026 in order to attend the scheduled event.

articles.originalTitle: Loro Piana Celebrates Finest Cashmere, Stages Exhibition - WWD
articles.title: Loro Piana Celebrates Finest Cashmere and Unveils Exhibition in New York
articles.excerpt: Held in New York, the 2025 cashmere awards honored exceptionally fine fibers while an immersive exhibition showcased the Italian house's heritage.
articles.content: The 2025 Loro Piana Cashmere of the Year Award celebrated a fiber fineness of 12.89 microns at an event held on Tuesday at The Brant Foundation in New York. The gathering also marked the unveiling of the “Master of Cashmere” exhibition, highlighting the Italian house's heritage and craftsmanship. Established in 2015, the annual accolade has contributed to improving the fineness of the fiber. The 11th edition honored three pairs of cashmere herders from Inner Mongolia. The first prize went to greasy cashmere weighing 135.8 kg with a 12.89 micron diameter, followed by the second prize for 87.1 kg at 13.01 microns and the third for 116 kg at 13.04 microns. A micron equals one-thousandth of a millimeter, whereas human hair measures 70 microns. Winners receive a financial reward per kilo alongside a silver comb symbolizing the gathering process. Executives emphasized that cashmere remains central to the brand identity. Through selective breeding programs and regional initiatives, the company aims to support herding communities and preserve local biodiversity. Loro Piana has been controlled by LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton since 2013.

articles.originalTitle: About the Punk to Pop exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Exhibition Explores Cultural Transformation from Punk to Pop
articles.excerpt: V&A South Kensington prepares to launch a comprehensive exhibition examining the explosion of music, art, and fashion between 1972 and 1985 in March 2027.
articles.content: Opening on 13 March 2027 at V&A South Kensington, the Punk to Pop exhibition re-examines the creative explosion across music, art, and fashion from 1972 to 1985. Spanning three acts and approximately 300 objects, the showcase traces a historical trajectory starting from glam rock and disco, moving through underground subcultures like punk, Goth, and New Romantics, and concluding with digital-era pop culture. Featuring prominent acts such as Sex Pistols, Grace Jones, Blondie, Joy Division, and Wham!, the exhibition demonstrates how self-determined artists responded to political turbulence and austerity. Highlighted items include album artwork by Jamie Reid, handwritten lyrics by Ian Curtis, Mick Jones's first guitar, and photographs by Andy Warhol. Through theatrical staging, fashion, and stage costumes, the multi-sensory presentation celebrates how music provided a platform for individuality, sexuality, and cultural experimentation during a transformative era.

articles.originalTitle: Probably by Camille Corot | Staircase in the Villa of Maecenas, Tivoli | L814 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Tivoli Landscape Attributed to Camille Corot at the National Gallery
articles.excerpt: A work thought to be by French artist Camille Corot from around 1826 in Italy is held in the National Gallery collection, featuring architectural sections and light contrasts.
articles.content: French artist Camille Corot produced 200 drawings and 150 oil studies during his stay in Italy between 1825 and 1828. Due to the scarcity of signatures on these sketches, attributions remain uncertain. The work titled Staircase in the Villa of Maecenas, Tivoli presents a visually satisfying vista from giant doors towards light coming through upper windows. Tivoli, a town northeast of Rome, was a frequent destination for artists due to its dramatic landscape. While signed Corot on the lower right, the sketch also bears the signature Granet in a likely more recent hand. Measuring 29.7 by 21.5 centimetres, the oil on paper laid on canvas is part of the Gere Collection on long-term loan to the National Gallery and is not currently on display. Corot's dedication to close observation of nature significantly influenced the later Impressionist approach to landscape painting.

articles.originalTitle: Best Government/Public Building: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse Wins Recognition
articles.excerpt: Built in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family courts into a central location.
articles.content: Situated in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family and children courts, probation services, and domestic violence units into a central urban location. The primary public entry is carved out under the upper floors to form a plaza as an extension of the streetscape. According to the submission, family courts require a de-escalating environment, addressed here by a multicolor art-glass two-story translucent screen on the public street wall and separate child-friendly playrooms in waiting areas. Constructing the massive complex in downtown Newark required meticulous coordination, including working within strict property lines, managing daily traffic flows, and minimizing disruptions to neighbors. The interior design divides spaces to separate hostile parties while accommodating sensitive zones, and integrates modern security with separate private entry points, holding cells, secure sallyports, and underground parking for judges. To counter unpredictable conditions, the project team relied on daily meetings and constant communication, allowing project managers, superintendents, and safety managers to address obstacles, coordinate daily tasks, and adapt in real time alongside cooperation with the city of Newark.
